entry_points.text: Boot self-checks run bitmap subtests and bitops probe setup, order validation, clearing, helper sweep with timing and completion logging; allocation failure aborts.
Builders emit self-checking shift, aliased-shift, pattern-enumeration and per-register immediate programs, publishing buffers and lengths into test objects.
Builders produce register-pair arithmetic, atomic and compare-swap checks, and wide-immediate loader sweeps over magnitudes and byte patterns.
Jump and staggered entries dedicate shared helpers to single conditions or taken-path templates, returning helper status.

hazards.text: Measured paths use volatile sinks, once-accessors and barriers against folding; builders return out-of-memory without touching descriptors and assert exact sizes so miscalculations trap at construction.

Staggered extent and allocation derive directly from the expected-result field without visible validation, and rewritten displacements depend on position arithmetic where scaling or entry errors would leave the image.
Out-of-truncation loads including nested traversals and metadata reads on empty packets must complete without fault and yield defined fallbacks rather than depending on packet content.

invariants.text: Narrow bitmap access and zero-length bitmap operations are safe against null maps and degenerate widths; adjacent narrow writes merge predictably and invalid-width reads are undefined. Sweeps cover all widths and offsets with timing.

Host helpers emulate ALU outcomes with narrowing and signed handling, map jump conditions across unsigned, signed, equality and bit-test families, derive operands around powers of two, and prefix logs with module names.

Maximum-size builders allocate a full buffer, fill a characteristic pattern, publish pointer and length into the case, and report allocation failure; variants cover returns, arithmetic chains, jumps, loads, atomic runs and extreme displacements.

Shift, pattern and ALU construction use sizing query then emission of self-checking sequences with host-compared expectations and fail-fast exit; dispatchers bind width, source kind and signedness while thin adapters fix operation.

Pair and atomic builders enumerate one hundred ordered pairs over ten registers with width seeds, check halves, memory and sentinels, use fixed emitter sizes and frame-pointer slots, form fail-fast guarded chains with null sizing, and install buffer and length.

Jump helpers adapt a shared pattern generator with width-specific emitters; staggered synthesis builds a header plus repeated guarded body linked by rewritten displacements, deriving extent from the expected result.
Construction relies on externally owned allocation, logging, bit, barrier, seed and instruction helpers specified elsewhere.

state_machines.text: Staggered images run header, deterministic chain walk updating and checking the result register, then termination; classic model holds accumulator, index, packet view, scratch and position with defined fallbacks for short inputs.

structs.text: A BPF case holds description, program union, flags, inputs, expectations, builder, error, fragments, stack depth and run count; flags use low bits for modes and higher bits for set selection under a mask.

Stable parameters: BPF limits 3 subtests, 1000 runs, 128 data bytes, 512 instructions, max immediate all bits set; packet type 3, mark 0x1234aaaa, hash 0x1234aaab, queue 123, VLAN tag all bits set with present 1, dev 577 and 588; eleven register aliases ending at frame pointer; bitops probes 4, 7, 11, 31, 88, sentinel 255, len 256, orders to 64; pattern extents 1 and 5 with one run; staggered ten runs with scaled even bound.

Each vector pairs label, program, mode tag, packet image and truncation to expectation list; classic mixes packet loads, arithmetic, moves, spills and guarded jumps with metadata reads, internal chains wide and narrow register arithmetic, endian variants preserve meaning.
